allocation.question: Can a credential-free task bank engineered for ASYMMETRIC discovery - multi-task sessions in which one-time session / resource / schema discovery is amortized or cached across tasks, and therefore materially different from the bounded-negative mandatory-discovery deterministic REST class - receive a PRE-FREEZE, arithmetically checkable dynamic-range certificate (B-COLD-RE-DERIVE and B-RETRIEVAL-SHAPED success_rate < 0.95 at novelty >= 0.50 on at least one family, matched correctness >= 0.80 for all arms, and a treatment/comparator distinction) so that it can serve as the reusable substrate that unblocks the flagship inheritance benchmark (B2), recording a bounded substrate-class negative and freezing nothing if the certificate is unsatisfiable on every credential-free substrate tested?
allocation.rationale: Runtime owns the B2 blocker, which is the binding constraint on the decisive benchmark: without a task bank where cold re-derivation and a retrieval-shaped comparator are not at the 1.0 ceiling, any SPIDER success or cost advantage has no dynamic range. The prior runtime thread (repairing the composite oracle for out-of-surface transfer) is a real scope bound on C-MEAS-VALID but is not on the critical path and has repeatedly produced MEASUREMENT_INVALID (lane same_failure_count 17, tunnel flag true), so spending the cycle there would re-litigate a bounded scope question while the decisive product test stays unrunnable. The active mandate instead emits a pre-freeze, arithmetically checkable certificate and freezes nothing if it cannot be satisfied, recording a bounded substrate-class negative. This is precisely the 'repair the prerequisite once instead of re-discovering ceiling degeneracy across lanes' move demanded by policy: it prevents a fourth rerun of the mandatory-discovery certificate that both EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 and the Product handoff explicitly exclude. The question is charter-eligible under C-MEAS-VALID (substrate validity) and needs neither a model endpoint nor the four-arm benchmark.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: The program's critical path is a serial three-blocker dependency that must be discharged before the one decisive four-arm benchmark (COLD vs INSTRUCTIONS vs RETRIEVAL vs SPIDER): B1 a shipped parameterized carrier, B2 a task bank where cold and retrieval are not at ceiling, B3 a same-model endpoint able to drive the minimal multi-step Web-agent test. None of the three readiness conditions holds in current accepted evidence, so the expensive C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON execution is not funded this cycle; instead the three blocker lanes are kept on exactly the prerequisite that removes their blocker. Product targets B1 (install the already-audited carrier, pinned at kernel.py sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 / git blob b15ed848, with a pre-freeze positive+negative certificate and promotion only on independent audit PASS). Runtime targets B2 (a credential-free asymmetric-discovery task bank with a pre-freeze, arithmetically checkable dynamic-range certificate, freezing nothing and recording a bounded substrate-class negative if unsatisfiable). Intel targets B3 (separate prompt underspecification from model incapacity on the local quantized 3B/7B endpoints, with the provisioning receipt and a bounded negative as exit). Graph's pivot off the substrate-blocked single-anchor D1V freshness route onto a design-contract-v2 C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE redesign is correct: goal-to-mechanism binding without internal ids is a component of the external-agent interface and is required for the SPIDER arm of the eventual benchmark, and three prior packets failed on control-plane/design defects (joint-authorship confound, reference arm provably identical to the candidate, controls incapable of failing, an unattainable ECE target, and the now-replaced V9 code-binding unsatisfiability), not on science. Physics and Frontier remain off the critical path: both are continued only because their active questions carry predeclared bidirectional decision value and are bounded, consistent with the standing audit recommendation that non-critical-path lanes proceed only under that condition. Physics varies the single untested factor (source vantage/egress) of the last accepted barrier result and will record a bounded operational negative if no second egress can be provisioned. Frontier re-asks the site-native-discovery acquisition question under design-contract v2 after v1 froze an empty sampling frame; on my judgement this is the terminal attempt on the acquisition-cost axis and must not be renamed again. No lane is idle; no parked thread warrants reopening; no experiment is left frozen-and-unfinished. The cumulative picture is unchanged since the global audit: reusable-procedure inheritance is plausible, universal Web dynamics are not established, and no net end-to-end cost reduction per successful partially novel task has yet been demonstrated for a real external agent.
